hook.line: Learn how to sell anything to anyone.
hook.visual: Black grid background with green glow; a famous film salesman on the phone fades in while 'LEARN HOW TO SELL ANYTHING TO ANYONE' builds word by word, then a light-leak flash into three coffee cups

beats.what: Movie cutaway of a slick salesman on the phone under the building title
'COFFEE SHOP' title and three cups (small, medium, large) slide in
Green bracket labels small and medium 'overpriced'
Thumbs-up icon lands under the large cup - the decoy pays off
Cut to 'PSYCHOLOGY FOR MARKETING' with a backpack
Watch and $49.99 price tag join the bag - bundle reframed as a free gift
'BRANDING IS EVERYTHING': plain tee at $4.99 next to a designer tee at $350
Closing line with CTA to follow for more

why_it_works: Every tip becomes a concrete price comparison on screen (cups at $5/$5.50/$5.90, tees at $4.99/$350), so the idea lands visually in one glance
A new graphic element arrives roughly every 2 s (30 events per minute measured), so the eye never rests on a static frame
Three tips in 30 s with bold green section titles give clear chapters and a short, loopable video (loop 0.956)
A recognisable film salesman in the first second borrows a status signal before any explanation
weaknesses: No face: little personal connection or creator identity beyond the handle
Small single-word captions in the middle are easy to miss next to the big titles
Third tip is asserted rather than explained; the CTA is generic
for_robert: Turn each claim into a side-by-side price or number comparison that builds in steps (items, then prices, then a bracket, then a verdict icon) - Fred could deliver the thumbs-up verdict instead of a sticker.
